newsitem.title: CHINA: HK airport plans HK$80bln in phase two spending.
newsitem.headline: HK airport plans HK$80bln in phase two spending.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority said it plans a HK$80 billion 15-year capital spending programme from 2001 onward in the second phase of development of the territory's new airport.

"In the next 15 years (from 2001)... we will be investing roughly HK$80 billion in capital expenditure and in replacing existing equipment," Airport Authority finance and commercial director Raymond Lai told Reuters in an interview.
"That is the money required to take us from 35 million capacity to 87 million capacity," he said.
Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok is due to open in April 1998 with capacity to handle 35 million passengers annually, rising over time to 87 million after a second runway is built.
While much of the funding for the new airport came from the government in the form of a HK$36 billion equity injection, Lai said the Authority would fund itself for the second phase.
All of the HK$80 billion would be borrowed through the capital markets, he said.
To date, the Authority has been a comparatively rare visitor to the capital markets.
In January last year it signed a HK$8.2 billion loan, and it is finalising a HK$5 billion note-issuance facility with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
Earlier this month, the Authority also launched a HK$3 billion revolving credit facility, which is expected to be increased to HK$4 billion when it closes.
Lai said he wanted to make use of a mixture of markets for the Authority's borrowing programme.
He said the U.S. market might be the Authority's first choice because of its long tenors and good cost of funds.
But he added that this might have changed by the time the Authority ultimately decided to borrow.
Lai said the Authority would also seek a credit rating before entering international bond markets.
